rows.title: Typical-orbit conjecture for interval-closed sets of products of two chains
rows.statement:
Fix a positive integer $m$. Let $r(n)$ be the fraction of interval-closed sets of $[m]\times[n]$ that belong to rowmotion orbits of size $m+n+1$. **Typical-orbit conjecture.** For every positive integer $m$, one has

$$
r(n)\to 1\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.
$$

This conjecture predicts that although rowmotion on interval-closed sets can have complicated behavior and large order, almost all interval-closed sets lie in orbits of the indicated size as $n$ grows. The source presents this as supported by experimental evidence and outlines a possible proof strategy, but does not establish it.
rows.source_name: Nadia Lafrenière, Joel Brewster Lewis, Erin McNicholas, Jessica Striker and Amanda Welch, “Interval-closed set rowmotion and homomesy on products of two chains”, arXiv:2505.04000 (2025).
rows.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04000

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

purpose: Independent adversarial qualification; no formal tools
